papers.title_en: CSPF: A Constrained Shared-Private Fusion Method for Non-Verifiable Preference Evaluation
papers.authors: Hehao Zhang, Danli Wang, Xinyuan Wang, Xuange Gao
papers.evidence: 将冻结奖励模型视为专家，采用共享-私有分解，类似于具有专家专业化的MoE
papers.tldr: 非可验证任务的偏好评估因缺乏客观标准而面临挑战，现有方法难以捕捉人类评价的多维度准则。本文提出CSPF方法，将多个异构冻结奖励模型作为互补评估器，学习融合其隐藏状态表示，并分解为共享和专家私有部分以平衡一致性与多样性。在LM-Arena和PPE基准上，CSPF在主要指标上超越单模型和多模型基线。该工作表明融合隐藏状态表示为非可验证偏好评估提供了更强大的表达基础。
papers.abstract_en: At present, reliable evaluation of non-verifiable tasks remains challenging. Existing approaches often fail to adequately capture the diverse evaluative criteria underlying human preferences in such tasks. To this end, we propose Constrained Shared-Private Fusion (CSPF), a fusion method that treats heterogeneous frozen reward models as complementary evaluators and learns to integrate their hidden-state representations under pairwise human-preference supervision. CSPF decomposes each expert signal into shared and expert-private representations, encouraging cross-expert alignment while preserving complementary viewpoints. Across experiments on LM-Arena target-domain adaptation and PPE out-of-distribution preference evaluation, CSPF achieves the best performance on the primary metrics among the evaluated single-expert reward-model, scalar-score multi-expert, and rubric-judge baselines. Overall, CSPF suggests that fusing hidden-state representations provides a more expressive basis for preference assessment, offering a practical route toward integrated evaluative signals for non-verifiable preference tasks.
